paragraphs: Vericel Corporation is a leading provider of advanced therapies for the sports medicine and severe burn care markets. We have a highly differentiated portfolio of cell therapy and specialty biologic products that combines innovations in biology with medical technologies. We were among the first companies to achieve commercial success in the complex field of cell therapies with treatments that use tissue engineering to regenerate skin and healthy knee cartilage. We currently market two U.S. Food and Drug Administration ("FDA") approved autologous cell therapy products and one FDA-approved specialty biologic product in the U.S. MACI® is an autologous cellularized scaffold product indicated for the repair of symptomatic, single or multiple full-thickness cartilage defects of the knee with or without bone involvement in adults. Since MACI's commercial launch, the product's FDA-approved labeling has provided for a treating surgeon to use MACI to treat a patient through an open surgical procedure. In August 2024, the FDA approved a supplemental Biologics License Application ("sBLA") expanding the MACI indication to add instructions for the arthroscopic delivery of MACI to the product's approved labeling. MACI Arthro® allows surgeons to evaluate and prepare the cartilage defect site as well as deliver the MACI implant through small incisions using custom-designed arthroscopic instruments developed by the Company ("MACI Arthro instruments"). MACI Arthro became commercially available in the U.S. during the third quarter of 2024, and the Company began selling MACI Arthro instruments at that time.

Epicel® is a permanent skin replacement Humanitarian Use Device ("HUD") indicated for the treatment of adult and pediatric patients with deep-dermal or full-thickness burns comprising greater than or equal to 30 percent of a patient's total body surface area ("TBSA"). We also hold an exclusive license from MediWound Ltd. ("MediWound") for the North American rights to NexoBrid® (anacaulase-bcdb), a topically-administered biological orphan product containing proteolytic enzymes, which is indicated for the removal of eschar in adult and pediatric patients with deep partial-thickness and/or full-thickness thermal burns.

Our objective is to expand our leadership position in the sports medicine and severe burn care markets and deliver a unique combination of revenue and profitability growth. To achieve this objective, we intend to:
•Continue to invest in potential MACI growth initiatives; •Seek clinical indication expansion for MACI, including for usage in additional joints;
•Launch MACI outside the United States in select markets, including the United Kingdom;
•Leverage our unique burn portfolio to expand the number of burn centers and surgeons using Epicel and NexoBrid; and;
•Generate positive operating income and cash flow.

We have a cell manufacturing facility in Cambridge, Massachusetts, which is currently used for U.S. manufacturing and distribution of MACI and Epicel. In January 2022, we entered into a lease agreement (as amended, the "Burlington Lease") to lease approximately 126,000 square feet of manufacturing, laboratory and office space in Burlington, Massachusetts. The Burlington facility is complete, and we are currently utilizing the facility's office space. Once validated, the facility's manufacturing component will eventually become the primary manufacturing facility for MACI and Epicel.

The manufacturing process for NexoBrid is conducted by MediWound, primarily at manufacturing locations in Israel. Certain raw materials utilized in NexoBrid's manufacture, including the supply of the active ingredient bromelain, are sourced from Taiwan.

On July 1, 2023, we renewed our long-term supply agreement with Matricel GmbH ("Matricel") for the supply of ACI-Maix collagen membranes used in the manufacture of MACI (the "Matricel Supply Agreement"). In the event Matricel is unable to supply the membranes, we may license the technology and procure the membranes from another source. The Matricel Supply Agreement provides that Matricel will supply the ACI-Maix membranes exclusively to us during the term of the agreement.

The Matricel Supply Agreement is effective until December 31, 2030, with an option to extend its term for three additional years to December 31, 2033. Thereafter, the Matricel Supply Agreement may be renewed for additional three-year periods.

Our current marketed products include two FDA-approved autologous cell therapies and one FDA-approved specialty biologic product. MACI is a third-generation autologous cellularized scaffold product indicated for the repair of symptomatic, single or multiple full-thickness cartilage defects of the knee with or without bone involvement in adults. In connection with our MACI product, we sell MACI biopsy kits, which are used by treating surgeons to obtain a sample of cartilage tissue, which is later sent to us. If a patient decides to move forward with MACI treatment, we subsequently use the cartilage sample to manufacture a MACI implant. When an orthopedic surgeon decides to treat a patient by implanting MACI through an arthroscopic approach, the surgeon may choose to use our custom MACI Arthro instruments during the procedure, which we sell by way of a separate transaction.

Epicel is a permanent skin replacement indicated for the treatment of adult and pediatric patients with deep-dermal or full-thickness burns comprising greater than or equal to 30 percent of a patient's TBSA. Both autologous cell therapy products, MACI and Epicel, are currently manufactured and marketed in the U.S. NexoBrid is a topically-administered biological orphan product containing proteolytic enzymes that is indicated for eschar removal in adult and pediatric patients with deep partial-thickness and/or full-thickness thermal burns. We hold exclusive license and supply agreements with MediWound to commercialize NexoBrid in North America.

Damage to cartilage in the knee can occur from acute or repetitive trauma from playing sports, exercising, work-related physical demands, or performing everyday activities. When damaged, cartilage in the knee does not usually heal on its own. If left untreated, cartilage defects can progress and lead to degenerative joint disease, osteoarthritis and potentially require total knee replacement, which is a poor option for younger and more active patients.

Our products represent new classes of therapy that the marketplace may not understand or accept. Furthermore, the success of our products is dependent on wider acceptance by the medical community.
If we do not effectively expand and train our direct sales force, we may be unable to add new customers or increase sales to our existing customers, and our business will be adversely affected.
Our success depends, in part, on the commercial success of NexoBrid for the removal of eschar in adult and pediatric patients with deep partial-thickness and/or full-thickness thermal burns.
Our inability to complete our product development activities successfully would materially limit our ability to operate or finance our operations.
If we do not keep pace with our competitors and with technological and market changes, our products will become less attractive or obsolete and our business may suffer.
We face risks associated with disruptive technologies, innovation and competition, including artificial intelligence.
Restrictions on the use of animal-derived materials could harm our product development and commercialization efforts.
If our licensing arrangement with MediWound is unsuccessful, our development of NexoBrid and its associated revenues may be limited.
Risks Related to the Manufacturing and Production of Our Products
paragraphs: The following summary highlights some of the principal risks that could adversely affect our business, financial condition or results of operations. This summary is not complete and the risks summarized below are not the only risks we face. These risks are discussed more fully further below. These risks include, but are not limited to, the following:
•We may experience significant quarterly and annual fluctuations in our results of operations due to a number of factors.
•Our operating results will be harmed if we are unable to effectively manage and sustain our future growth or scale our operations.
•We may not be able to manage inventory in an effective and efficient manner, which could adversely affect our results of operations.
•Although we reported net income for the years ended 2024 and 2025, we have incurred losses in the past and may not achieve consistent profitability for some time or at all.

•Our products and product development programs are based on novel technologies and are inherently risky, which may decrease the chances of regulatory approval and could have a material effect on our financial condition and operating results.

The Company operates its business primarily in the U.S. in one reportable segment - the research, product development, manufacture and distribution of cellular therapies and specialty biologics for use in the treatment of specific conditions.

MACI is a third-generation autologous chondrocyte implantation ("ACI") product indicated for the repair of symptomatic, single or multiple full-thickness cartilage defects of the knee with or without bone involvement in adults.

Our target audiences are orthopedic surgeons who self-identify and/or have formal specialty training in sports medicine, and a subpopulation of general orthopedic surgeons who perform a high volume of cartilage repair procedures involving the knee. Our MACI commercial team consists of individual sales representatives that regularly engage with our target audience. The team is divided into geographic regions and is managed by a senior sales leadership team. A vast majority of the largest commercial payers in the U.S. have a formal medical policy that provides benefit coverage for treatment with MACI. With respect to private commercial payers that have not yet approved a medical policy for MACI, we often obtain approval on a case-by-case basis.

MACI consists of autologous cultured chondrocytes, which are human-derived cells that are obtained from the patient's own cartilage, and which are seeded onto resorbable Type I/III collagen membrane. Since MACI's commercial launch, the product's FDA-approved labeling has provided for a treating surgeon to use MACI to treat a patient through an open surgical procedure. In August 2024, the FDA approved a supplemental Biologics License Application ("sBLA") expanding the MACI indication to add instructions for the arthroscopic delivery of MACI to the product's approved labeling, permitting the repair of single or multiple full-thickness cartilage defects of the knee up to 4 cm2 in size via an arthroscopic approach. MACI Arthro provides a less invasive technique compared to the open arthrotomy approach and allows surgeons to evaluate, prepare and treat the cartilage defect and deliver the MACI implant, under direct arthroscopic visualization and, should the surgeon so choose, to use specialized and custom-designed instruments (the "MACI Arthro instruments") through small incisions or portals. The arthroscopic delivery of MACI may increase the ease of MACI's use for physicians and may reduce both the length of the procedure as well as procedure-induced trauma, which may result in a reduction of a patient's post-operative pain and accelerate a patient's recovery. MACI Arthro became commercially available in the U.S. during the third quarter of 2024 and we began selling MACI Arthro instruments at that time. We have experienced strong surgeon interest in the MACI Arthro technique since its launch. To date, more than 900 surgeons have participated in Company-sponsored education and training programs concerning the arthroscopic approach. We believe that the availability of MACI Arthro provides a significant growth opportunity for the overall MACI business, as we have already seen a significant increase in both MACI biopsies and implants from those surgeons who have engaged in MACI Arthro training and education programs. In conjunction with the launch of MACI Arthro, we have expanded our target surgeon base from 5,000 to 7,000 to include orthopedic surgeons that perform high volumes of knee cartilage repair surgeries, predominantly through arthroscopic procedures.

We also are focused on delivering MACI treatment to patients suffering from cartilage damage in the ankle. Following an application to the FDA, we received Investigational New Drug ("IND") clearance for MACI's use in the ankle during the second quarter of 2025, and during the fourth quarter of 2025 initiated a Study of MACI in Patients Aged 17 to 65 with Symptomatic Chondral or Osteochondral Defects of the Talus ("MASCOT"). MASCOT is a two-year prospective, multicenter, two-arm, parallel group open-label trial in which a total of 309 subjects, aged 17 to 65 will be randomized 2:1 to receive a one-time treatment in the talus with MACI or arthroscopic bone marrow stimulation. MASCOT is the first randomized, controlled clinical trial evaluating MACI for the treatment of Osteochondral Lesion of the Talus ("OLT"). There are approximately 165,000 ankle resurfacing procedures conducted in the U.S. each year. Approximately 66,000 of those patients each year are considered clinically appropriate for MACI by surgeons. We estimate that approximately 18,000 of those patients suffer from larger ankle cartilage lesions, resulting in an increase of MACI's addressable market. If approved, we believe MACI's label expansion allowing its use to repair cartilage defects in the ankle will be a significant long-term growth driver for the product in the coming years.

Finally, our Burlington facility, discussed more fully above, is designed to meet both U.S. and global manufacturing requirements, which provides strategic flexibility to potentially commercialize MACI outside the U.S., and we are currently evaluating introducing MACI in additional geographies. We are currently focused on obtaining regulatory and marketing approval for MACI in the United Kingdom through the Medicine and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency ("MHRA") and, if successful, anticipate commercializing MACI in the United Kingdom in 2027.

Epicel is a permanent skin replacement for deep-dermal or full-thickness burns comprising greater than or equal to 30 percent TBSA. Epicel is regulated by the FDA's Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research ("CBER") under medical device authorities, and is the only FDA-approved cultured epidermal autograft product available for large total surface area burns in both adult and pediatric patients. Epicel was designated as a HUD in 1998 and an HDE application for the product was

submitted in 1999. HUDs are devices that are intended for diseases or conditions that affect fewer than 8,000 individuals annually in the U.S., and, for certain HUDs, the amount a manufacturer may charge for the product's use is restricted.

Epicel is not price-restricted in this manner because in 2016, the FDA approved our HDE supplement to revise the labeled indications of use for Epicel to specifically include pediatric patients, thus allowing Epicel to be sold for profit. The product label also specifies that the probable benefit of Epicel, mainly related to survival, was demonstrated in two Epicel clinical experience databases and a physician-sponsored study comparing outcomes in patients with large burns treated with Epicel relative to standard care.

paragraphs: Vericel Corporation 是運動醫學與嚴重燒傷照護市場的領先供應商。我們擁有高度差異化的細胞治療與特殊生物製品組合，結合生物學創新與醫療科技。我們是首批在細胞治療複雜領域取得商業成功的公司之一，提供使用組織工程技術再生皮膚與健康膝蓋軟骨的治療方案。我們目前在美國市場行銷兩種美國食品藥物管理局（"FDA"）核准的自體細胞治療產品，以及一種 FDA 核准的特殊生物製品。MACI® 是一種自體細胞化支架產品，用於修復有症狀、單一或多重全層軟骨缺損的膝蓋，且可能伴隨骨頭受損的成人患者。自 MACI 開始商業銷售以來，該產品的 FDA 核准標籤允許治療外科醫生透過開刀手術使用 MACI 治療患者。2024 年 8 月，FDA 核准了補充生物製品許可申請（"sBLA"），擴展 MACI 的核准適應症，以增加透過關節鏡方式施用 MACI 的說明至產品核准標籤。MACI Arthro® 讓外科醫生可以評估並準備軟骨缺損部位，並透過小切口使用本公司（"MACI Arthro 裝置"）設計的關節鏡儀器施用 MACI 置入物。MACI Arthro 在 2024 年第三季於美國市場開始商業銷售，本公司在該時段開始銷售 MACI Arthro 裝置。

Epicel® 是一種永久性皮膚替代品人道使用裝置（"HUD"），用於治療成人及兒童患者，其深層皮膚或全層皮膚燒傷面積大於或等於患者總體表面積（"TBSA"）的 30%。我們也擁有 MediWound Ltd.（"MediWound"）在北美地區的獨家授權，使用 NexoBrid®（anacaulase-bcdb），一種局部施用的生物孤兒產品，含有蛋白酶，用於去除成人及兒童患者的深層部分皮膚或全層熱傷的焦痂。
我們的目標是擴大在運動醫學與嚴重燒傷照護市場的領導地位，並實現獨特的收入與獲利成長組合。為達成此目標，我們打算：
•持續投資潛在 MACI 成長計畫；•尋求 MACI 的臨牀適應症擴張，包括用於其他關節的使用；
•在美國以外的特定市場推出 MACI，包括英國；
•善用我們獨特的燒傷產品組合，擴大使用 Epicel 和 NexoBrid 的燒傷中心與外科醫生數量；以及；
•產生正向營運獲利與現金流。

我們在麻薩諸塞州劍橋市設有細胞製造廠，目前用於美國 MACI 和 Epicel 的製造與分銷。2022 年 1 月，我們簽訂了一項租賃協議（經修正後，稱為 " Burlington 租賃"），租賃麻薩諸塞州 Burlington 約 126,000 平方英尺的製造、實驗室與辦公室空間。Burlington 廠區已經完工，我們目前使用該廠區的辦公室空間。一旦驗證完成，該廠區的製造零組件將最終成為 MACI 和 Epicel 的主要製造廠區。
NexoBrid 的製造過程由 MediWound 進行，主要在以色列的製造場地進行。NexoBrid 製造所使用的某些原材料，包括活性成分 bromelain 的供應，來自臺灣。
我們於 2023 年 7 月 1 日與 Matricel GmbH（"Matricel"）續簽了長期供應協議（"Matricel 供應協議"），用以供應用於 MACI 製造的 ACI-Maix 膠原膜。若 Matricel 無法供應這些膜片，我們可能取得技術授權並從其他來源購入。Matricel 供應協議規定，在協議有效期間，Matricel 將獨家供應 ACI-Maix 膜片給我們。
Matricel 供應協議的有效期至 2030 年 12 月 31 日，並有選擇權可將協議期限延長三個額外年份至 2033 年 12 月 31 日。協議到期後，可再續簽三個年期。

我們目前上市的產品包括兩種美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）核准的自體細胞療法，以及一種 FDA 核准的專門生物製品。MACI 是第三代自體細胞化支架產品，用於修復成人膝蓋的症狀性單一或多重全層軟骨缺損，且可能伴隨骨頭損傷。與 MACI 產品相關，我們銷售 MACI 穿刺套件，用於治療外科醫生取得軟骨組織樣本，之後會送回我們。若患者決定進行 MACI 治療，我們會使用該軟骨樣本製造 MACI 置換物。當骨科外科醫生決定透過關節鏡手術植入 MACI 治療患者時，外科醫生可能選擇在手術中使用我們的 MACI 關節鏡儀器，這些儀器我們透過獨立交易銷售。

Epicel 是一種永久性皮膚替代品，用於治療成人及兒童患者因深度真皮或全層燒傷所造成的傷害，且傷及面積大於或等於患者體表面積（TBSA）的 30%。自體細胞療法產品 MACI 和 Epicel 目前均在美國製造與銷售。NexoBrid 是一種局部使用的生物孤兒藥品，含有蛋白酶，用於去除成人及兒童患者的深度部分層或全層熱傷造成的焦痂。我們與 MediWound 維持獨家授權與供應協議，以在北美地區商業化 NexoBrid。
膝蓋軟骨損傷可能由急性或反覆的運動、運動、工作相關體力需求或日常活動造成。當軟骨受損時，通常無法自行癒合。若未治療，軟骨缺損可能惡化，導致退化性關節疾病、關節炎，甚至可能需要進行全膝關節置換手術，這對年輕且活動力強的患者來說是不理想的選擇。

paragraphs: Vericel Corporation 為運動醫學與嚴重燒傷照護市場的先進療法主要供應商。我們擁有高度差異化的細胞治療與專門生物製品組合，結合生物學創新與醫療科技。我們是首批在細胞治療複雜領域取得商業成功的公司之一，提供利用組織工程再生皮膚與健康膝關節軟骨的治療方案。我們目前在美國市場行銷兩項美國食品藥物管理局（"FDA"）核准的自體細胞治療製品與一項 FDA 核准的專門生物製品。MACI® 是一種自體細胞化支架製品，用於治療成人膝關節之症狀性單一或多重全層軟骨缺損，包含或不包含骨頭受損。自 MACI 開始商業銷售以來，該製品的 FDA 核准標籤允許治療外科醫生透過開刀手術方式使用 MACI 治療病患。2024 年 8 月，FDA 核准補充生物製品許可申請（"sBLA"），擴展 MACI 的核准適應症，新增 MACI 透過關節鏡方式施用的說明至產品核准標籤。MACI Arthro® 讓外科醫生能評估並準備軟骨缺損部位，並透過小切口使用本公司（"MACI Arthro 儀器"）所開發的專用關節鏡儀器施用 MACI 置入物。MACI Arthro 於 2024 年第三季開始在美國市場商業銷售，本公司於此時開始銷售 MACI Arthro 儀器。

Epicel® 是一種永久性皮膚替代品人道使用裝置（"HUD"），用於治療成人與兒童患者之深層皮膚或全層燒傷，其面積大於或等於患者總體表面積（"TBSA"）的 30%。我們也持有 MediWound Ltd.（"MediWound"）在北美地區的獨家授權，以銷售 NexoBrid®（anacaulase-bcdb），一種局部施用的生物孤兒製品，含有蛋白酶，用於去除成人與兒童患者之深層部分厚度與/或全層熱傷的壞死組織。
我們在馬薩諸塞州劍橋市設有細胞製造廠，目前用於美國 MACI 與 Epicel 的製造與分銷。2022 年 1 月，我們簽訂租賃契約（經修正後，稱為 "Burlington 租賃"），租賃馬薩諸塞州伯靈頓市約 126,000 平方英尺的製造、實驗室與辦公室空間。伯靈頓廠房已完工，我們目前使用該廠房的辦公室空間。一旦驗證完成，該廠房的製造部分將成為 MACI 與 Epicel 的主要製造廠房。
NexoBrid 的製造過程由 MediWound 進行，主要在以色列的製造廠進行。NexoBrid 製造所使用的部分原料，包括活性成分 Bromelain 的供應，來自臺灣。

我們目前行銷的產品包括兩項 FDA 核准的自體細胞治療製品與一項 FDA 核准的專門生物製品。MACI 是第三代自體細胞化支架製品，用於治療成人膝關節之症狀性單一或多重全層軟骨缺損，包含或不包含骨頭受損。與 MACI 產品相關，我們銷售 MACI 病理採樣套件，用於治療外科醫生取得軟骨組織樣本，之後送至我們處。若病患決定進行 MACI 治療，我們隨後使用該軟骨樣本製造 MACI 置入物。當骨科外科醫生決定透過關節鏡方式植入 MACI 治療病患時，外科醫生可選擇在手術中使用我們的 MACI Arthro 儀器，我們透過獨立交易銷售此儀器。

Epicel 是一種永久性皮膚替代品，用於治療成人與兒童患者之深層皮膚或全層燒傷，其面積大於或等於患者總體表面積（"TBSA"）的 30%。自體細胞治療製品 MACI 與 Epicel 目前均在美國製造與行銷。NexoBrid 是一種局部施用的生物孤兒製品，含有蛋白酶，用於去除成人與兒童患者之深層部分厚度與/或全層熱傷的壞死組織。我們與 MediWound 簽訂獨家授權與供應契約，以在北美地區商業化 NexoBrid。本公司主要在美國經營業務，屬於一個應報告分部 - 研究、產品開發、製造與分銷用於治療特定疾病的細胞療法與專門生物製品。
MACI 是第三代自體軟骨細胞植入（"ACI"）製品，用於治療成人膝關節之症狀性單一或多重全層軟骨缺損，包含或不包含骨頭受損。
我們的目標客羣為自認並/或具正式專門訓練於運動醫學的骨科外科醫生，以及一小部分執行大量軟骨修復手術的普通骨科外科醫生。我們的 MACI 商業團隊由個別銷售代表組成，定期與目標客羣互動。團隊按地理區域分區，由高階銷售領導團隊管理。美國最大的商業保險機構中，絕大多數都有正式的醫療政策，提供 MACI 治療的保險給付。針對尚未核准 MACI 醫療政策的私人商業保險機構，我們通常透過個案方式取得核准。

MACI 係由自體培養軟骨細胞所組成，這些細胞為人體來源，從患者的軟骨中取得，並種植於可吸收之 Type I/III 膠原膜上。自 MACI 開始商業銷售以來，產品經 FDA 批准的標籤允許治療外科醫生透過開放性手術程序使用 MACI 來治療患者。2024 年 8 月，FDA 批准了 MACI 的補充生物製品許可申請（"sBLA"），擴展 MACI 的適應症，新增於產品批准標籤中關於透過關節鏡方式施用 MACI 的說明，允許透過關節鏡方式修復膝蓋單一或多處全層軟骨缺損，大小至多 4 平方公分。MACI Arthro 提供較開放性關節切開術更為侵入性較低的技術，讓外科醫生可在直接關節鏡視覺下評估、準備及治療軟骨缺損並施用 MACI 置入物，若外科醫生選擇，也可透過小切口或 portals 使用專用且客製化設計的儀器（"MACI Arthro 儀器"）。MACI 的關節鏡施用方式可能增加對醫師使用 MACI 的便利性，並可能減少手術時間及手術引起的創傷，進而減少患者的術後疼痛並加速患者的復原。MACI Arthro 於 2024 年第三季開始在美國商業銷售，我們在該時段開始銷售 MACI Arthro 儀器。自 MACI Arthro 開始銷售以來，我們已觀察到外科醫生對 MACI Arthro 技術的強烈興趣。截至目前為止，已有超過 900 名外科醫生參與本公司舉辦的教育與培訓課程。我們認為 MACI Arthro 的可用性為 MACI 事業帶來顯著的成長機會，因為我們已觀察到參與 MACI Arthro 培訓與教育課程的外科醫生，其 MACI 穿刺與植入數量均有顯著增加。配合 MACI Arthro 的上市，我們已將目標外科醫生人數從 5,000 名擴展至 7,000 名，包含執行大量膝蓋軟骨修復手術的骨科外科醫生，主要透過關節鏡手術進行。

我們同時也致力於將 MACI 治療提供給患有腳踝軟骨損傷的患者。在向 FDA 提出申請後，我們於 2025 年第二季獲得 Investigational New Drug（"IND"）許可，允許 MACI 用於腳踝，並於 2025 年第四季啟動一項針對 17 至 65 歲有症狀性軟骨或軟骨軟骨缺損患者的 MACI 研究（"MASCOT"）。MASCOT 是一項兩年期的前瞻性、多中心、雙臂、平行組、開放標籤試驗，總共 309 名 17 至 65 歲受試者將被隨機以 2:1 的比例分配，接受一次性的 MACI 治療或關節鏡骨髓刺激治療。MASCOT 是第一項評估 MACI 用於治療腳踝軟骨軟骨損傷（"OLT"）的隨機對照臨牀試驗。每年美國約進行 165,000 個腳踝修復手術。其中約 66,000 名患者每年被外科醫生認為適合使用 MACI。我們估計其中約 18,000 名患者患有較大的腳踝軟骨損傷，導致 MACI 的可接觸市場增加。若獲得批准，我們認為 MACI 的標籤擴張允許其用於修復腳踝軟骨缺損，將為產品在未來幾年帶來顯著的長期成長動力。
最後，我們位於 Burlington 的廠房，如上所述更詳細說明，設計符合美國與全球製造需求，這提供了戰略彈性，使我們有可能在美國以外地區商業化 MACI，目前我們正在評估在其他地區引入 MACI。目前我們專注於取得 MACI 在英國的監管與市場批准，透過英國藥物與醫療器材監管局（"MHRA"），若成功，預計於 2027 年在英國商業化 MACI。

Epicel 是一種永久性皮膚替代品，用於治療深層真皮或全層燒傷，其覆蓋面積大於或等於 30% 的 TBSA。Epicel 由美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）的生物製品評估與研究中心（"CBER"）以醫療器材管理，是目前唯一經 FDA 批准可用於成人及兒童患者的大面積總體表面積燒傷的培養表皮自體移植產品。Epicel 於 1998 年被指定為罕見疾病醫療器材（HUD），並於 1999 年提交了產品的 HDE 申請。
於1999年提交。HUDs為用於治療或緩解影響美國每年少於8,000名個體之疾病或症狀之裝置，且對某些HUDs，製造商可收取之產品使用費用上限受到限制。
Epicel 不受此種費用限制，因為在 2016 年，FDA 批准我們的 HDE 補充申請，修改 Epicel 的標籤適應症，特別包含兒童患者，因此允許 Epicel 以獲利方式銷售。產品標籤也說明 Epicel 的可能效益，主要與存活率相關，已在兩個 Epicel 臨牀經驗資料庫及一項由醫師主導的比較研究中顯示，該研究比較使用 Epicel 治療大面積燒傷患者與標準照護的結果。

headings: 與我們營運相關的風險
我們可能因多種因素而導致每季及每年營運結果出現顯著波動。
若我們無法有效管理並持續未來成長或擴大營運規模，將會對我們的營運結果造成損害。
若我們無法以有效且高效的方式管理存貨，可能會對我們的營運結果產生不利影響。
雖然我們在2024年12月31日及2025年12月31日結帳年度報出淨收入，但我們過去曾出現虧損，可能在一段時間內或完全無法實現穩定的獲利。
我們的產品代表新的治療類別，市場可能不理解或接受。此外，我們產品的成功取決於醫療界更廣泛的接受度。
若我們無法有效擴展並培訓我們的直接銷售團隊，我們可能無法增加新客戶或提高現有客戶的銷售額，並對本公司業務造成不利影響。
本公司成功在一定程度上取決於 NexoBrid 在成人及兒童深度部分厚度及/或全層熱傷患者去除壞死組織方面的商業成功。
若我們無法成功完成產品開發活動，將會嚴重限制本公司運營或籌資運營的能力。
若我們無法跟上競爭對手及科技與市場變化的腳步，我們的產品將變得較不具吸引力或過時，並可能對本公司業務造成影響。
我們面臨與顛覆性科技、創新及競爭相關的風險，包括人工智慧。
對動物衍生材料使用的限制可能對我們的產品開發及商業化工作造成影響。
若我們與 MediWound 的授權協議未能成功，將可能限制我們開發 NexoBrid 及其相關收入。
與本公司產品製造及生產相關的風險
paragraphs: 下列摘要說明了若干可能對我們業務、財務狀況或營運成果產生負面影響的主要風險。此摘要並非完整，下列總結的風險並非我們唯一面臨的風險。這些風險在後續內容中會有更詳細的說明。這些風險包括但不限於以下內容：
•我們可能因多種因素而經歷顯著的季度與年度營運成果波動。
•若我們無法有效管理並維持未來的成長或擴大營運規模，將會對我們的營運成果造成損害。
•我們可能無法以有效且高效的模式管理存貨，這可能會對我們的營運成果產生負面影響。
•雖然我們在2024年及2025年財務年度報導了淨收入，但我們過去曾出現虧損，並可能在一段時間內或完全無法實現穩定的獲利。
•我們的產品與產品開發計畫基於創新技術，本質上具有風險，這可能會降低獲得監管機構核准的機率，並對我們的財務狀況與營運成果產生重大影響。
